assumptions: Arrival context: my daughter sent me the link on my iPad because the family is thinking about how to mark my husband's 65th, possibly a few days away with three generations including my mother, who uses a walking frame.
I read top to bottom, as the persona card says, and forwarded it to my husband with questions.
HTML comments, image slot notes and fact markers are invisible to me as a reader.

Business details (fees, commissions, on-the-ground support, transfers, room blocks, Wedded Privileges, phone lines) are deliberately deferred for this post, so I have not asked for edits about them. Where they matter to me they sit in unanswered_questions only.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes an exact sentence from the draft
Every suggested edit 'old' value is an exact, unique substring of 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Margaret (62, Melbourne, practical, cautious with money)
No invented brand facts; anything the page does not say is listed as an unanswered question
No suggested edit adds prices, fees, commissions, vendor names, statistics words or em dashes, or asks how the fee is worked out
Deferred business details (fees, on the ground, transfers, room blocks, Wedded Privileges, phone lines) not requested as edits
Did not invent problems; positives recorded where the draft already works for me

open_questions.question: The page never mentions deposits or cancellation terms in the venue questions. My suggested edit adds a plain question for the reader to ask the venue (no prices). Is that acceptable within the deferral rules?
The Wedded Concierge paragraph says 'for Australian couples' on a birthday article. Should this read 'clients' so it does not feel like a wedding page pasted in?

first_impression.reaction: Sensible start. It asks the right question first, who the person is and what they'd enjoy, rather than selling me a theme. No silly slang, short paragraphs, I can read it on the iPad without my glasses slipping. I kept going because my daughter sent it and I wanted to see whether it dealt with the older ones travelling.

journey.quote: The celebrations that land well start with the guest of honour.
journey.reaction: Agreed. My husband would hate a fuss, so this is the right place to start.

journey.quote: A candle is an open flame and can easily ignite anything combustible nearby, so keep the area around each one clear of linen, florals and paper, and use sturdy holders made of material that cannot burn, as the [SA Metropolitan Fire Service candle fact sheet](https://www.mfs.sa.gov.au/community-safety/safety-and-education/fact-sheets/candles2/mfs-fact-sheet-candles.pdf) sets out.
journey.reaction: Good, practical advice and I like that it points to the fire service. But that is one very long sentence. I had to read it twice.

journey.section: A long lunch or garden party
journey.quote: Daytime suits a mixed guest list, from young children to older relatives.
journey.reaction: Yes. My mother is not staying up until midnight. Nice to see someone think of that.

journey.quote: Plan for comfort first: short journeys, rooms without stairs where needed, and one evening when everyone sits down together.
journey.reaction: This is the line that made me take the page seriously. Rooms without stairs is exactly what I'd be asking about for Mum.

journey.quote: Think about mobility and travel comfort before you think about the setting.
journey.reaction: Thank you. Most of these articles show a cliff-top terrace and never ask how Nana gets there.

journey.section: Choose the date and book the anchor event
journey.quote: What will you confirm in writing, and when?
journey.reaction: Good question to have on the list. But there's nothing about the deposit: how much is held, whether I get it back if we cancel or the date moves. That is the first thing I'd ask and it isn't there.

journey.section: Choose the date and book the anchor event
journey.quote: How are dietary and accessibility needs handled, and are candles allowed?
journey.reaction: Accessibility is mentioned, which I appreciate, but it's vague. I'd want to know if every room we'll be in can be reached without steps.

journey.quote: On the day, the host should be a guest.
journey.reaction: Lovely thought, and true. I spent my own 60th in the kitchen.

journey.quote: Declare everything upfront, including pre-existing health conditions, or the policy may be void.
journey.reaction: This is the sort of thing I'd forward to my husband and my sister. Proper advice, and it links to the government site rather than some insurer.

journey.quote: guests travelling from the United States can work through the [international travel checklist from the US Department of State](https://travel.state.gov/en/international-travel/planning/checklist.html).
journey.reaction: Not relevant to us, but I can see why it's there if family come from overseas. Skipped past it.

journey.section: Where everyone stays and one hosted dinner
journey.quote: Ask the venue or hotel whether airport transfers can be arranged and how guests reach the dinner and return.
journey.reaction: Good. Getting Mum from the airport to the hotel is half the worry.

journey.section: Where everyone stays and one hosted dinner
journey.quote: Wedded Concierge plans milestone birthdays through the same Wedded Advisor process: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person, Australian time, Australian dollars: that's what I want. But 'Australian couples' on a birthday page threw me. It's my husband's birthday, not a wedding. And I don't know what 'the same Wedded Advisor process' is, it assumes I've read something else.

journey.section: Planning a milestone birthday with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: 'Agreed in writing before any work begins' is the most reassuring sentence on the page. That's what I'd point my husband to.

unanswered_questions: Who do I ring if something goes wrong while we're away, in our time? (Understood this is deferred for this post.)
Is the money we pay protected if a venue or hotel overseas folds or cancels?
Whose name are the contracts in, ours or Wedded Concierge's, and are they in English?
Can I speak to the Wedded Advisor on the phone before anything is booked?
Does Wedded Concierge actually do birthdays regularly, or is it mainly weddings?

turn_offs_found.quote: What will you confirm in writing, and when?
turn_offs_found.why: The venue checklist mentions writing but never deposits or cancellation. My turn-off is 'no mention of contracts, deposits or who is responsible', and deposits are missing entirely from the advice.

would_share_with: My husband, with the travel insurance section and the closing paragraph circled
My sister, who is helping with Mum's travel

cta_reaction.why: 'Start a conversation' is gentle, which I like, and the fee in writing helps. I would click if we decide on going away rather than a lunch at home, but I'd want it to lead to a phone call with a real person, not a form, before I pay anything.

top_3_changes: Add a deposit and cancellation question to the venue checklist so the page covers who holds the money and what happens if plans change.
Change 'Australian couples' to 'Australian clients' in the Wedded Concierge paragraph so a birthday reader doesn't feel they've landed on a wedding page.
Make the accessibility question specific (step-free access to every space) and split the long candle sentence so it reads easily.

suggested_edits.old: - What will you confirm in writing, and when?
suggested_edits.new:
- What deposit is needed, when is the balance due, and what happens to the deposit if you cancel or the date moves?
- What will you confirm in writing, and when?
suggested_edits.reason: Deposits and cancellation are the first thing a cautious payer asks, and the checklist never mentions them. This is a question for the reader to ask the venue, with no prices or brand claims added.

suggested_edits.old: How are dietary and accessibility needs handled, and are candles allowed?
suggested_edits.new: How are dietary and accessibility needs handled, including step-free access to every space you will use, and are candles allowed?
suggested_edits.reason: Older relatives with walking frames need step-free routes to the terrace, dining room and bathrooms. 'Accessibility needs' alone is too vague to ask a venue.

suggested_edits.old: quoting in AUD for Australian couples
suggested_edits.new: quoting in AUD for Australian clients
suggested_edits.reason: On a birthday article, 'couples' makes it feel like copied wedding copy and makes me wonder whether birthdays are really looked after.

suggested_edits.old: A candle is an open flame and can easily ignite anything combustible nearby, so keep the area around each one clear of linen, florals and paper,
suggested_edits.new: A candle is an open flame and can easily ignite anything combustible nearby. Keep the area around each one clear of linen, florals and paper,
suggested_edits.reason: The original sentence is very long. Splitting it keeps the same facts and source but is easier to read on an iPad.
